metaTitle: Best Large Capacity Air Fryers in 2026
metaDescription: Seven large air fryers from 8 to 14 quarts, dual zone, single basket and oven style, compared on usable space, heating speed, wattage and cleaning.
expertTake: The Ninja DZ401 with two 5 quart baskets is the best all round pick for most families, because it cooks two foods at once. The DZ071 MegaZone is the flexible pick if you also want one 7 quart basket. The Chefman 12 quart oven is the choice for rotisserie and multi-rack meals. If you cook for one or two people, skip large units, which waste counter space and preheat energy.
introParagraphs: A large air fryer is a small convection oven built around a powerful fan and a heating element. The quart rating on the box measures the cavity, not the usable cooking surface, so two machines with the same label can hold very different amounts of food. The shape, whether a basket, a pair of drawers or a rack oven, changes what you can cook.

This guide explains how to size an air fryer by food and household, how dual zone, single basket and oven designs differ, and what to check on wattage and cleaning. Start with the picks above for the short list, then read the reviews below to match a machine to your counter and your meals.

products.name: Ninja Foodi DZ401 10 Qt DualZone XL Air Fryer

specList.label: Zones
specList.value: Two independent baskets, each with a fan and heater

specList.label: Modes
specList.value: Air fry, broil, roast, bake, reheat, dehydrate

products.description:
The DZ401 is the large air fryer that fits how most households actually cook, which is two things at once. Two independent 5 quart baskets each have their own fan and heating element, so a protein can cook at one temperature while a side cooks at another. Smart Finish times the two zones to end together, and Match Cook copies settings across both for a full 10 quart batch.

Compared with a single big basket, the split design is the trade you must understand. Each zone is only 5 quarts, so a whole large chicken or a wide pizza does not fit in one basket the way it does in the 12 and 14 quart oven-style Chefman units. In exchange you get no flavor mixing, no waiting for a second batch and a smaller footprint than an oven-style machine. Against the smaller DZ201, you gain 2 quarts of total capacity and larger baskets.

The nonstick coating is listed as PFAS free and the crisper plates are dishwasher safe, which helps the chore that makes owners stop using air fryers. Pull the baskets out and wipe the heating chamber now and then, since grease collects on the element housing. Leave a few inches of clearance behind the unit for exhaust air. The maker says it cooks two 6 pound chickens up to 30 percent faster than a conventional oven, which is a claim, but the real benefit is the convenience of dual zones.
products.bestFor: Families of four to six who cook a protein and a side at the same time.
pros: Two independent 5 qt baskets cook two foods two ways
Smart Finish makes both zones end at the same moment
Match Cook copies settings across zones for a full 10 qt batch
Nonstick surface is listed as PFAS free and easy to clean
cons: Each basket is only 5 qt, so very large items do not fit
Larger counter footprint than a single basket model
Two baskets and two crisper plates mean more parts to wash

specList.label: Capacity

products.description:
The MegaZone is the air fryer that answers the main complaint about dual-basket machines, which is that each side is too small for a big piece of food. A removable divider turns the cooking space into two 3.5 quart zones, and taking it out gives one 7 quart basket that fits a 4 pound pork roast with vegetables. The same machine can therefore act as a single large fryer or a dual unit.

It uses two heating fans that work together and the DualZone controls, including Smart Finish and Match Cook, so the two sides can be timed together when the divider is in place. The maker quotes a 450F maximum and says it cooks a whole meal about 40 percent faster than a conventional oven. Compared with the 10 quart DZ401, total capacity is lower, but the flexibility is higher. Against the single-basket 9 quart Chefman, it costs more but offers the split option.

Handling is simple. The basket and crisper plates are nonstick and dishwasher safe, and the divider is a separate piece you wash and store. Each 3.5 quart zone holds about 2 pounds of food, so for a crowd you will want the single-zone mode. Leave clearance behind the machine and shake or flip food partway for even results.
products.bestFor: Cooks who want one machine that can be a big single basket or two small zones.

Fits a 4 lb pork roast with vegetables in single zone mode
Smart Finish and Match Cook still work with the divider
Two heating fans cook faster than a single fan design
cons: Total 7 qt is smaller than the 10 qt and 12 qt units
Each divided zone is only 3.5 qt, about 2 lb of food
The loose divider is one more part to wash and store

products.name: Chefman Crispinator 8 Qt Air Fryer with Dial Controls

specList.label: Functions
specList.value: Six: air fry, bake, broil, dehydrate, keep warm and more

specList.label: Controls
specList.value: Top mounted dials with LED shake reminders

products.description:
The Crispinator is an 8 quart single-basket air fryer built around a high-powered DC motor that reaches 450F. A DC motor spins faster and can vary speed, which is why the maker says it improves heating times and runs quietly. It is a horizontal, low-profile basket designed to let you fill it in one flat layer, which helps with wings, fries and fish where airflow around each piece matters.

Dial controls on top set time and temperature, and LED notifications tell you when to shake or flip, which are practical touches for those who dislike touchscreens. A built-in viewing window with an interior light lets you watch cooking without opening the basket and losing heat. Compared with the Ninja dual-zone units, you cook only one thing at a time, but you get a bigger single space and a simpler layout. The 5 year assurance is the longest of the Chefman models in this lineup.

Cleaning is easy, because the nonstick basket and interior are top-rack dishwasher safe. At 1700 watts on a standard 120 volt outlet, avoid running it on the same circuit as a microwave or toaster. The listing also mentions a 2024 Red Dot Design Award, which is about looks, not performance. If you want to cook two foods at once, choose a Ninja instead.
products.bestFor: Cooks who prefer dials over screens and want a long warranty on a single basket.
pros: Dial controls are simple to use with wet or oily hands
LED shake reminders prompt flipping for even crisping
Viewing window and light let you check without opening
Five year assurance is the longest of the Chefman models
cons: Only one basket, so side dishes need a second batch
Maximum 8 qt is smaller than the 9 qt and larger units
1700W draw needs a circuit not shared with other appliances

products.name: Chefman TurboFry 9 Qt Air Fryer with Window

specList.label: Functions
specList.value: Seven: air fry, broil, dehydrate, bake, reheat, keep warm, frozen

specList.label: Motor
specList.value: DC motor, up to 40 percent faster than other Chefman air fryers (maker claim)

products.description:
The 9 quart TurboFry is the largest single-basket model here and the biggest step above the 8 quart Crispinator. A DC motor drives air at up to 450F, and the maker claims it cooks up to 40 percent faster than other Chefman air fryers, though that comparison is against the brand's own machines. The listing says it feeds up to seven people, which is optimistic, but a 9 quart basket genuinely suits a large family's fries or wings in one batch.

Seven functions include a Frozen mode that starts at a low temperature to thaw and then crisps. A Keep Warm setting holds food for up to 30 minutes, and a Shake Reminder prompts a flip. A viewing window means you can check doneness without losing heat. Compared with the Crispinator, you get one extra quart and a touchscreen instead of dials, but the warranty is only 1 year against 5.

Because the basket is wide, spread food in a single layer rather than piling it, or the crisping suffers. Wash the basket and rack in the top rack of the dishwasher. At 1750 watts it is one of the highest-draw machines here, so give it its own outlet circuit when possible. If you need two foods at once, choose a Ninja.
products.bestFor: Large families who cook one big batch and want the most single-basket capacity.

Frozen mode thaws and then crisps in a single program run
Keep Warm holds food for up to 30 minutes after cooking
Viewing window and shake reminder help with even results
cons: Only a one year assurance, shorter than the Crispinator
1750W draw is the highest of the basket models listed here
The 40 percent faster claim compares only to other Chefman units

products.name: Chefman 12 Qt 5-in-1 Air Fryer Oven with Rotisserie

specList.label: Temperature
specList.value: 95F to 400F, Hi-Fry to 450F for the last two minutes

specList.label: Functions
specList.value: Air fry, bake, dehydrate, rotisserie, roast, reheat

specList.label: Includes
specList.value: Three racks, rotisserie spit and forks, retrieval tool, drip tray

products.description:
The 12 quart Chefman is an oven-style air fryer, which means a rack-based cavity with a door, not a drawer basket. That shape is why it can take a whole chicken on a rotisserie spit, a 9 by 13 inch pan or three racks of food at once, jobs that a drawer fryer cannot do. A window and interior light let you check progress, and the removable drip tray catches grease.

Temperature runs from 95F to 400F, with a Hi-Fry button that raises it to 450F for the last two minutes to crisp chicken tenders and fries. Twelve presets and a touch screen make it easy to use, and the included accessories cover racks, a rotisserie spit and forks and a retrieval tool. Compared with the 14 quart Chefman, it is smaller and shallower, which helps on a crowded counter. Against the Ninja drawers, it cooks more food on more levels but needs more preheating space and room.

Oven-style units are deeper and wider than baskets, so measure your counter and the clearance above. Air circulates across racks, so food on the top rack browns first, and you should rotate trays halfway. The 1 year assurance is short. If you mainly cook fries and wings, a basket model is simpler, but for roast chicken and sheet pan meals this is the type to choose.
products.bestFor: Families who roast a chicken or cook on multiple racks and want a toaster oven replacement.
pros: Rotisserie spit turns a whole chicken for even browning
Three racks hold several foods at the very same time
Hi-Fry setting boosts heat to 450F for the last two minutes
Includes drip tray and a retrieval tool for hot racks
cons: Deeper and wider than a basket air fryer on the counter
Maximum steady temperature is 400F, below the 450F baskets
Maker lists only a one year assurance on this unit

products.name: Chefman 14 Qt 6-in-1 Air Fryer Oven with Rotisserie and Touchscreen

specList.label: Functions
specList.value: Air fry, bake, broil, reheat, dehydrate, rotisserie

products.description:
The 14 quart Chefman is the largest cavity in this comparison, with three rack positions so a main and sides can cook together. Like the 12 quart unit it is an oven-style design with a windowed door, but the extra capacity makes it a closer substitute for a countertop oven. A removable rotisserie spit with a ROTATE function and a fetch tool lets you cook a chicken or shawarma.

A touchscreen controls the six functions and a 90F to 400F range. Because the interior is bigger, it takes up more counter space than any basket, so measure the width, depth and height before ordering. Compared with the 12 quart Chefman, it adds two quarts and one function, the broil setting, for a similar warranty. Against the Ninja DZ401, it gives much more total volume, but you cook one temperature at a time unless you use racks.

Plan the cleaning. The drip tray, racks and spit are dishwasher safe in most cases, but the cavity needs wiping after greasy cooks. A 1700 watt element should not share a circuit with a microwave. This is the model if you want maximum volume and are willing to give up counter space.
products.bestFor: Large families or entertainers who want a high-capacity oven that air fries.

specList.label: Zones

specList.label: Modes
specList.value: Air fry, broil, roast, bake, reheat, dehydrate

specList.label: Fry load

products.description:
The DZ201 is the original DualZone design and the least expensive Ninja here. Two independent 4 quart baskets each have a cyclonic fan and a rapid heater, with a temperature range of 105F to 450F. The maker says the 8 quart total holds up to 4 pounds of French fries or chicken wings.

Smart Finish and Match Cook work the same way as on the bigger models, so you can cook two foods two ways and finish together, or copy settings across both zones for a full batch. Compared with the DZ401, each zone is 1 quart smaller, which matters for chicken thighs or a pan of vegetables. Against the single-basket Chefman 8 quart, you get two zones for a similar total volume, but each side is half the size.

Cleaning is straightforward, since the baskets can be washed by hand or in the dishwasher and the crisper plates are nonstick. Leave clearance behind and avoid overfilling, because crowded baskets lose crispness. It suits a family of three or four, or a couple who like cooking two foods at once. If you often cook for six, move up to the DZ401.
products.bestFor: Couples and small families who want dual baskets without paying for the largest model.

buyingCriteria.explanation: The quart rating is a cavity volume, and the usable area for food is smaller because of the heating element, the basket walls and the airflow gap. Shape matters too: a wide, low basket like the Chefman Crispinator holds more flat items such as wings and fish than a deep round one. A 4 pound chicken needs height, a 13 inch pizza needs width. Check whether your typical meal fits, not just the headline number.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Choose a layout: basket, dual zone or oven
buyingCriteria.explanation: A single basket like the Chefman 9 quart is simplest and cooks one big batch. A dual-zone model such as the Ninja DZ401 has two 5 quart baskets with independent controls. An oven-style unit like the Chefman 12 quart or 14 quart has racks and a rotisserie. Basket and dual zone suit fries, wings and weeknight meals, while oven style suits a roast chicken or sheet pan dinners.

A rough rule is about one quart per person for a basket, so 8 to 10 quarts suit four to six people. The Ninja DZ201 at 8 quarts total suits three or four, while the DZ401 at 10 quarts suits five or six. Oven-style units at 12 to 14 quarts suit large families who cook roasts. Buying far above your needs wastes counter space and preheat time.

Large air fryers draw 1,700 to 1,750 watts, close to the limit of a 15 amp household circuit, which supplies about 1,800 watts. The Chefman TurboFry lists 1750W and the Crispinator 1700W. Running one on the same circuit as a microwave or kettle can trip a breaker. Plug it into its own outlet and avoid light extension cords.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Look at temperature range and speed
buyingCriteria.explanation: A 450F maximum, as on the Ninja DZ models and the Chefman baskets, crisps frozen foods better than a 400F maximum, which is the ceiling on the oven-style Chefman units. Fan design matters too, because a stronger fan moves hot air faster across the food. The Ninja DZ071 uses two heating fans, and the Chefman TurboFry uses a DC motor. Treat faster than a conventional oven claims as marketing.

Dishwasher safe baskets and crisper plates, as listed on the Ninja and Chefman units, determine whether you keep using the machine. A large air fryer also needs clearance behind it for exhaust and room above it, and oven-style units can be 16 inches deep. Measure your counter and cabinet clearance before buying. Nonstick coatings wear, so avoid metal utensils.

specDecoder.meaning: Quarts measure the volume of the cooking cavity or basket. A 10 quart unit is roughly 9.5 liters. It does not equal the usable food area, which is lower because of the element and airflow clearance.
specDecoder.watchFor: A dual unit rated at 10 quarts is two 5 quart baskets, not a single 10 quart basket. The Ninja DZ401 is split this way.

specDecoder.meaning: Watts measure the heating power. Most large air fryers use 1,700 to 1,750 watts. More watts does not always mean faster cooking, because airflow matters.
specDecoder.watchFor: A circuit rated 15 amps supports about 1,800 watts. Sharing with another appliance can trip it.

specDecoder.meaning: The highest setting of the unit. 450F crisps frozen foods and sears meat, while 400F suits baking and roasting. Heat is delivered by fan-driven air.
specDecoder.watchFor: The 12 and 14 quart Chefman ovens top out at 400F, with a 450F Hi-Fry only for the last two minutes on the 12 quart.

specDecoder.meaning: DualZone gives two baskets with independent fans and heaters. Smart Finish times them to end together, and Match Cook copies settings. Together they cook two different foods in the same time.
specDecoder.watchFor: Each zone is half the total. The DZ401 has 5 quart baskets, so total capacity does not mean any single large item fits.

specDecoder.meaning: PFAS are a class of chemicals sometimes used in nonstick coatings. A PFAS free label means the coating avoids them. The Ninja DZ401 lists its nonstick as PFAS free.
specDecoder.watchFor: A PFAS free coating still wears. Avoid abrasive pads and metal tools to extend its life.

howWeEvaluated.title: Usable capacity and layout
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared total quarts and the layout, from the 14 quart oven-style Chefman to the 8 quart DZ201. We favored layouts that matched real meals, such as a rotisserie for chicken and dual baskets for protein and sides.

howWeEvaluated.title: Heating power and speed
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared wattage, maximum temperature and fan design. The Ninja DZ models and Chefman baskets reach 450F, and the oven-style Chefman units reach 400F. We treated faster than oven claims as unverified.

howWeEvaluated.title: Controls and features
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at dials, touchscreens, shake reminders and presets. The Crispinator dials and the DZ401 Smart Finish are the standouts, and the Chefman TurboFry has a frozen mode. We weighed features that change cooking results.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cleaning and counter fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared dishwasher safe parts, depth and clearance. Basket models take less counter space, and oven styles need the most. We noted the extra parts of the DZ071 divider.

howWeEvaluated.title: Warranty and lineup value
howWeEvaluated.description: We placed each unit by capacity and extras. The Crispinator has a 5 year assurance while other Chefman models list 1 year. We matched each machine to a household size.

howToChoose.subheading: Basket vs Dual Zone vs Oven
howToChoose.intro: The layout changes what you can cook.

cards.label: Single basket and dual zone
cards.text: The Chefman TurboFry and Crispinator are single baskets, and the Ninja DZ201, DZ401 and DZ071 are dual zone. Baskets cook fast and crisp well, and dual zones let you cook two foods at once. They suit fries, wings, cutlets and weeknight meals.

cards.label: Oven style
cards.text: The Chefman 12 and 14 quart units have racks, a door and a rotisserie. They fit whole chickens, pans and multi-rack meals. They are larger and top out at 400F, but replace a toaster oven.

howToChoose.note: Choose a basket or dual zone for fast, crisp weeknight cooking. Choose an oven style for roasts, rotisserie and bigger pans.

howToChoose.intro: The interface and support matter after the first month.

rows: Sync two foods to finish together

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A family needs capacity, speed and easy cleaning. Look for at least 8 to 10 quarts, dishwasher safe parts and a way to cook two items at once. A wide basket helps with flat foods.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Ninja DZ401 is the best fit because of its 10 quart total and Smart Finish. The Chefman 14 Qt oven suits a family that cooks roasts, and the TurboFry 9 Qt suits big batches of one food.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Spend more if you cook most nights for four or more. The Ninja DZ401 and DZ071 add dual zones and flexibility that save time, and the Crispinator adds a long assurance.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Save if you air fry only occasionally. The Chefman TurboFry or the Ninja DZ201 cover typical meals, and a bigger machine would sit unused.

maintenance.task: Wash the basket and crisper plate
maintenance.why: Grease bakes onto the nonstick and smokes next time. Wash by hand or in the dishwasher as the manual allows.
Grease splatters collect near the element and can smoke. Wipe with a damp cloth when cool.

maintenance.task: Clean the air intake and exhaust
maintenance.why: Dust and grease block airflow and cut performance. Keep clearance behind the unit.
Metal utensils and scouring pads scratch nonstick coatings. Use silicone or wood.
A high-wattage appliance needs a good cord and outlet. Do not use thin extension cords.

maintenance.task: Descale or clean the drip tray
maintenance.interval: Every few uses on oven styles
maintenance.why: The drip tray collects grease. Empty it to prevent smoke and odor.

faq.q: Is a dual zone air fryer better than a single basket?
faq.a: It depends on how you cook. Dual zone suits protein and a side at once, finishing together. A single basket suits one big batch and often holds a larger single item. Large single baskets like the 9 quart Chefman suit crowds of one food.

faq.q: Do I need an oven style air fryer?
faq.a: Choose oven style if you roast chickens, cook on pans or want to replace a toaster oven. Oven styles are larger and top out at 400F in this group. For fries and wings, a basket is simpler and often crisper.

faq.q: How much food does a 10 quart air fryer hold?
faq.a: It depends on the layout. The DZ401 has two 5 quart baskets, so each holds about half the total. Spread food in a single layer and do not overfill, since crowded food steams instead of crisping.

faq.q: Are nonstick air fryer baskets safe?
faq.a: Nonstick coatings are safe when used as directed and kept undamaged. The DZ401 lists a PFAS free coating. Avoid scratching and replace a basket whose coating flakes.

faq.q: Will a big air fryer trip my breaker?
faq.a: It might. Large models draw 1,700 to 1,750 watts, close to what a 15 amp circuit supplies. Do not run them with a microwave or kettle on the same circuit.

faq.q: Do air fryers use less oil?
faq.a: Yes. They use hot moving air, so food crisps with little or no added oil. Results differ from deep frying, and wet batter does not work well. Spray a little oil for the best browning.
